# Packman and the repo_man Bootstrap

Packman is the package manager that bootstraps repo_man and all repo-tools. It is not a repo-tool itself -- it is an external dependency that repo_man relies on for fetching tools, managing dependencies, and providing the Python runtime.

## Bootstrap Chain

When a user runs `repo.sh` or `repo.bat`, this chain executes:

```text
repo.sh / repo.bat
  |
  ├── Sets OMNI_REPO_ROOT environment variable
  ├── Reads repo-cache.json (if exists) to set PM_PACKAGES_ROOT
  ├── Invokes: tools/packman/python.sh tools/repoman/repoman.py "$@"
  |
  └── repoman.py
        |
        ├── repoman_bootstrap()
        │     ├── _path_checks()          # Warn about whitespace/OneDrive in paths
        │     ├── _prep_cache_paths()      # Set PM_PACKAGES_ROOT, PIP_CACHE_DIR, UV_CACHE_DIR
        │     └── _pull_optional_deps()    # Pull repo-deps-{suffix}.packman.xml if exists
        |
        ├── pull_deps()
        │     ├── packmanapi.pull("deps/repo-deps.packman.xml")
        │     └── Add all returned paths to sys.path
        |
        └── omni.repo.man.main(REPO_ROOT)  # Start repo_man
```

## Entry Point Scripts: repo.sh and repo.bat

Every repo-tools-consuming repository has `repo.sh` and `repo.bat` at its root (occasionally in a subdirectory for multi-layered repos). These are the **only** way to invoke repo-tools:

- **`repo.sh`** -- For POSIX-compatible shells (Linux, macOS, Git Bash on Windows, WSL)
- **`repo.bat`** -- For Windows shells (CMD, PowerShell)

```bash
# Linux / macOS / Git Bash / WSL
./repo.sh build -r

# Windows CMD or PowerShell
.\repo.bat build -r
```

These scripts bootstrap the entire environment: they locate Packman's Python, pull dependencies, set up `sys.path`, and then invoke `omni.repo.man.main()`. Running Python or the tools directly without these scripts will fail.

## Files a Consumer Repo Needs

To use repo-tools, a repository needs these bootstrap files:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `repo.sh` | Entry point for POSIX shells (Linux, macOS, Git Bash, WSL) |
| `repo.bat` | Entry point for Windows shells (CMD, PowerShell) |
| `tools/packman/` | Packman distribution (python, bootstrap scripts) |
| `tools/repoman/repoman.py` | repo_man bootstrapper script |
| `tools/repoman/repoman_bootstrapper.py` | Bootstrap helpers (cache, optional deps) |
| `deps/repo-deps.packman.xml` | Declares which repo-tools to install |
| `repo.toml` | Repository configuration (can be minimal) |

## Tool Availability

A Packman package can ship **multiple tools**, many disabled by default. For example, pulling `repo_man` gives you access to `repo update`, `repo deps`, `repo pydeps`, `repo cache`, `repo ai`, and more -- but most require `enabled = true` in `repo.toml` to activate.

To see what tools a package provides:
```bash
cat _repo/deps/repo_man/repo_tools.toml | grep -E "^\[repo_|command =|enabled ="
```

To enable a tool that defaults to disabled:
```toml
# In repo.toml
[repo_pydeps]
enabled = true
```

To see all currently enabled tools:
```bash
repo --help
```

**Caveat:** `repo --help` pulls **all** declared tools from Packman (because help text requires importing each tool). This is slow on first run. If you just need to check one tool, use `repo <command> --help` instead -- it only pulls that tool.

See the **Tool Patterns** skill for the full enable/disable mechanism and a list of common built-in tools.

## Packman Dependency XML Format

Dependencies are declared in `deps/repo-deps.packman.xml`:

```xml
<project toolsVersion="5.0">
  <dependency name="repo_man" linkPath="../_repo/deps/repo_man">
    <package name="repo_man" version="..."/>
  </dependency>
  <dependency name="repo_test" linkPath="../_repo/deps/repo_test">
    <package name="repo_test" version="..."/>
  </dependency>
  <dependency name="repo_lint" linkPath="../_repo/deps/repo_lint">
    <package name="repo_lint" version="..."/>
  </dependency>
</project>
```

### Elements

| Element | Attributes | Description |
|---------|------------|-------------|
| `<project>` | `toolsVersion` | Root element |
| `<dependency>` | `name`, `linkPath` | Declares a dependency; `linkPath` is where the package is symlinked |
| `<package>` | `name`, `version`, `platforms` (optional) | Package to fetch from Packman remote |
| `<source>` | `path` | Local source path override (for development) |

### Platform-Specific Packages

```xml
<dependency name="my_tool" linkPath="../_repo/deps/my_tool">
  <package name="my_tool" version="1.0.0" platforms="windows-x86_64,linux-x86_64"/>
</dependency>
```

### Token-Based Versions

Packman XML preserves `${...}` tokens in version strings. These are resolved by consuming tools at runtime:

```xml
<package name="python" version="3.10.10+nv1-${platform}"/>
```

Common tokens used in versions: `${platform}`, `${config}`, `${platform_target}`, `${platform_target_abi}`.

### Source Paths (Local Development)

To develop against a local copy of a dependency instead of the Packman version:

```xml
<dependency name="repo_lint" linkPath="../_repo/deps/repo_lint">
  <package name="repo_lint" version="..."/>
  <source path="C:/src/repo_lint"/>
</dependency>
```

When a `<source>` element is present, Packman uses the local path instead of fetching the package.

## The `_repo/deps/` Directory

After `packmanapi.pull()`, each dependency gets a symlink:

```text
_repo/deps/
  repo_man    -> /c/packman-repo/chk/repo_man/<version>
  repo_test   -> /c/packman-repo/chk/repo_test/<version>
  repo_lint   -> /c/packman-repo/chk/repo_lint/<version>
```

These directories are added to `sys.path`, making tools importable. This is how repo_man discovers `repo_tools.toml` files and skill directories in each tool.

## Optional / Private Dependencies

Repositories can have private dependencies that are only pulled in certain environments:

```toml
# In repo.toml
optional_deps_suffix = "nv"    # Default if omitted
```

This causes the bootstrapper to also pull `deps/repo-deps-nv.packman.xml` (if it exists). If the file is missing, it is silently skipped.

This is how internal tools like `repo_nv` (NVIDIA-specific config) are pulled without affecting public consumers who don't have `repo-deps-nv.packman.xml`.

## The `repo deps` CLI

Manipulate Packman XML files from the command line:

### Add a dependency

```bash
repo deps packman add my_package --version 1.2.3
repo deps packman add my_package --version 1.2.3 --linkpath ../_repo/deps/my_package
repo deps packman add my_package --version "1.0-${platform}" --platform windows-x86_64
```

### Update a dependency version

```bash
repo deps packman update my_package --version 2.0.0
repo deps packman update my_package --version latest    # Search for latest
```

### Remove a dependency

```bash
repo deps packman remove my_package
repo deps packman remove my_package --version 1.2.3     # Remove specific version
```

### Link to local source (for development)

```bash
repo deps packman source my_package --sourcepath C:/src/my_package
```

### Remove source link

```bash
repo deps packman unsource my_package --sourcepath C:/src/my_package
```

### Import dependencies from another file

```bash
repo deps packman import --importfile deps/host-deps.packman.xml --package my_package
```

### Create a new empty deps file

```bash
repo deps packman new --projectfile deps/custom-deps.packman.xml
```

### Generate preconfigured deps files

```bash
repo deps packman generate all
repo deps packman generate my_configured_file
```

All commands default to operating on `deps/repo-deps.packman.xml`. Use `--projectfile` to target a different file.

## Caching with repo-cache.json

Repositories can override Packman cache locations by creating `repo-cache.json` in the repo root:

```json
{
  "PM_PACKAGES_ROOT": "_cache/packman",
  "PIP_CACHE_DIR": "_cache/pip",
  "UV_CACHE_DIR": "_cache/uv"
}
```

- **Relative paths** are relative to the repository root
- **Absolute paths** are used as-is
- This file is read very early in the bootstrap (before repo_man loads)

The `repo cache` command can generate and manage this file:

```bash
repo cache set         # Create repo-cache.json with default paths
repo cache clear       # Remove cached files
```

## Python Dependency Vendoring

Each repo-tool can vendor its Python dependencies (pip/UV packages). These are stored in the Packman cache with a hash key:

```text
${PM_PACKAGES_ROOT}/chk/${tool_name}_deps/${requirements_hash}/${platform}/${python_version}/
```

A symlink is created at `${root}/_repo/deps/${tool_name}_deps/` pointing to the cache.

Dependencies are defined in a tool's `requirements.txt` and automatically installed during `validate_dependencies()` (called from the tool's `__init__.py`). If the requirements hash changes, dependencies are reinstalled.

## Packman API (from repo-tools code)

```python
import packmanapi

# Pull all dependencies from a project file
deps = packmanapi.pull("deps/repo-deps.packman.xml")
# Returns: {"repo_man": "/path/to/cached/package", ...}

# Install a single package
packmanapi.install(name="my_package", version="1.0", link_path="_repo/deps/my_package")
```

The `omni.repo.man.deps` module wraps Packman with additional features:
- Platform-aware fetching
- Thread-safe locking
- MD5 integrity verification
- UV/pip fallback for Python deps
- Source path resolution

## Key Environment Variables

| Variable | Set By | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `OMNI_REPO_ROOT` | `repo.sh`/`repo.bat` | Repository root path |
| `PM_PACKAGES_ROOT` | `repo-cache.json` or system default | Packman package cache root |
| `PM_INSTALL_PATH` | Packman bootstrap | Where Packman itself is installed |
| `PIP_CACHE_DIR` | `repo-cache.json` | pip cache directory |
| `UV_CACHE_DIR` | `repo-cache.json` | UV cache directory |

## Common Patterns

### Adding a new tool to a repository

```bash
repo deps packman add <package_name> --version <version> --linkpath ../_repo/deps/<package_name>
```

Then run any `repo` command to trigger the pull. Consult your organization's package registry or tool documentation for available versions.

### Checking what version of a tool is installed

```bash
cat _repo/deps/<package_name>/VERSION
```

### Updating a tool

```bash
repo deps packman update <package_name> --version <new_version>
```

### Developing against a local tool copy

```bash
repo deps packman source repo_lint --sourcepath C:/src/gl/r/ov/repo/batch_ops/repo_lint
# To stop using local source:
repo deps packman unsource repo_lint --sourcepath C:/src/gl/r/ov/repo/batch_ops/repo_lint
```
